attacksRun.evidence: The namedCatalog review pin b2673ab2 is my own verdict from earlier in this session, and OBL-G18-NAMED-CATALOG rests on it, so I cannot corroborate my own ACCEPT. What makes this case cleaner than some others in the sweep is that the join does not rely on the catalog's standing alone: it quotes the three-member list inline, and I checked that quotation against live G18 v2 rather than against the catalog or my verdict. The obligation's substance therefore stands on harness bytes. All three review pins here are single-reviewer Claude 2 verdicts with no Codex counterpart.

Seven obligations, each bucketed exactly once across summary's five lists, none duplicated or omitted. The two obligations with leftoverDesign true are exactly the two carrying not-capable-of-riding standings. All four summary flags match the obligation bodies, and liveGateOwners for DR-G18 is used consistently.

observationsNotFindings: Quoting the three-member list inline in the obligation reason is a small choice that does real work. Most joins in this sweep cite a catalog by digest and describe it; this one reproduces the list itself, so a reader can check the naming claim against the harness without opening the catalog at all. It is also what let me verify the obligation without leaning on my own prior verdict.

The file 08 token is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW rather than the OPEN carried by most sibling joins in this sweep, and the join states it correctly. That is worth noting because a token copied from a sibling would have been wrong here, and because DR-107 being further along than DR-112 or DR-120 changes what a later recording of this join would mean.

OBL-ENCODING-RESERVED is untouched from v1 and remains the harder of the two open obligations: live G18 v2 journalHonesty cites file 04 that the concrete lock, journal and lease mechanism is open, so no amount of naming or fixture work closes it without a separate mechanism decision. The join assigns that to a later implementation successor rather than to this row.

All three review pins are single-reviewer with no Codex counterpart, one of them mine. DR-107's design standing has the same shape I have flagged on DR-112, DR-120 and DR-122 - honest at every artifact, thin in aggregate, and visible only from the coordinator's position.

All 11 recordedInputs and eight pins recompute. The file 08 token is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, which is what DR-107 actually carries rather than the OPEN most siblings carry.
